verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you have to register your own in the Dev Dashboard. A custom-distribution app works on your dev store or one merchant's store (or one Plus organization) in minutes, with no review. Installing on many stores requires public distribution, a one-time App Store registration fee and App Approval review. Protected customer data (name, email, phone, address) adds its own review for public apps.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a custom app; 1-3 days to prepare a public app for submission (compliance webhooks, protected-data answers, listing)
verdict.approval_wait: None for custom distribution. For public distribution, about 5-10 business days for the first review (reported by third parties, not stated officially).

gates.name: Custom distribution / development store
gates.unlocks: You create the app in the Dev Dashboard, install it on your own development store, and connect through Composio.
limits: New apps must be created in the Dev Dashboard. Custom apps can no longer be created in the Shopify admin (since 1 Jan 2026).
Apps installed only on development stores can use customer data without a protected-data review, but you still have to select the data fields.
Online tokens expire after 24 hours. Offline tokens last as long as the app stays installed.

gates.name: Custom distribution (single store or Plus organization)
gates.unlocks: A specific merchant's store (or the stores in one Plus organization) installs the app from an install link you generate. No approval is needed.
limits: Limited to one store, one Plus organization, or development stores.
You can't use Shopify's app billing to charge merchants.
The distribution method can't be changed after you pick it.
Shopify has no unlisted, no-review option for public apps. Unpublished apps were deprecated in 2019, and community reports say limited-visibility public apps still go through review.
Protected customer data levels 1 and 2 are always available to custom apps.

gates.name: Public distribution (Shopify App Store, full or limited visibility)
gates.unlocks: Any merchant can install the app on their store.
limits: Requires a one-time App Store registration fee and App Approval review against all app requirements.
Protected customer data (levels 1 and 2) needs its own review for public apps, and Shopify may run a detailed data protection review.
Third-party guides say three mandatory compliance (GDPR) webhooks are required and checked by automated tests.
Some scopes need Shopify Support approval before you can declare them.
gates.time_to_reach: About 5-10 business days after submission (unofficial figures), plus your preparation time

steps.title: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Create or sign in to a Shopify Partner account, then open the Dev Dashboard. To install the app on many stores later, the app must belong to a Partner organization, because only those apps get a Distribution card.
gotchas: Apps created inside a store's own organization skip distribution and install only on that store.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Dev Dashboard. You can no longer create a legacy custom app in the Shopify admin.

steps.title: Trim the scope list
steps.detail: Start from Composio's default Shopify scopes and remove any your agent doesn't use. A write scope already includes read access. Leave out approval-required scopes (such as read_apps or read_shopify_payments) and read_all_orders unless you really need them.
gotchas: Customer and order scopes bring in protected-data rules for public apps.
Shopify restricts scopes when it sees no legitimate use for the data.

steps.title: Configure and release a version (App URL, scopes, redirect URL)
steps.detail: On the app's Versions tab, set the App URL, the access scopes, and the allowed redirection URL, then release the version. The redirect URI has to match the one Composio sends exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URLs appear to be set per version (reported by the community, not confirmed in official docs). Release a new version whenever you change them.
Two Composio callback URLs show up in different places. Use the one shown in your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose a distribution method
steps.detail: On the app's home page, use the Distribution card. Pick Custom for one store, one Plus organization, or dev stores (no review). Pick Public for any merchant (requires review and a registration fee).
gotchas: Custom apps can't use Shopify billing.

steps.title: Install on your dev store or generate an install link
steps.detail: For custom distribution, enter the store's myshopify.com or admin.shopify.com domain and optionally restrict the app to that store. Then click Generate link and send the install link to the store owner. For your own dev store, install from the app's Home page.
gotchas: If you use customer data on a dev store, you still have to select the data fields first.

steps.title: Add the credentials to Composio
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, go to Settings and copy the Client ID and Client Secret. In Composio, create a Shopify auth config with your own credentials and the trimmed scopes. Composio uses the per-shop authorize URL https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize.
gotchas: Credentials exist only in the Dev Dashboard, not in shopify.app.toml.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Connect your dev store through Composio, then confirm the redirect succeeds and an access token comes back. Shopify checks the redirect URL against the allowed list, and the flow must validate the HMAC, state and shop hostname.
gotchas: Online tokens expire after 24 hours. Use offline tokens for agents that run in the background.

steps.title: Implement compliance webhooks and the post-install redirect
steps.detail: For public apps, implement the three mandatory compliance (GDPR) webhooks. After merchants approve scopes, send them to your app's UI, not a login page.
gotchas: A community report describes an app rejected in automated OAuth checks because the redirect went to a login page.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard, open the app and go to API access requests. Request protected customer data and give your reasons, select each protected field with a reason, and complete the Data protection details. An agent can draft the justifications.
gotchas: Level 2 data (name, email, phone, address) has seven more requirements, including an access log and encrypted backups.

steps.title: Register for the App Store and submit for review
steps.detail: Pay the one-time App Store registration fee, work through the self-assessment checklist in the Partner Dashboard, and submit the app to the App Approval team. You can choose full or limited visibility.
gotchas: Limited visibility still requires review, according to community reports.

steps.title: Wait for App Approval review
steps.detail: Reviewers install the app on a test store and check the OAuth flow, the compliance webhooks, billing, the UI, and whether your declared scopes match the API calls you make. Feedback arrives by email and is tracked per requirement in the Partner Dashboard.

requirements.item: Allowed redirection URL that exactly matches Composio's callback
requirements.detail: The redirect URI must be listed as an allowed redirection URL for the app.
Choose Custom or Public. You can't change it later.

Level 1 covers data minimization, merchant transparency, purpose and retention limits, and encryption. Level 2 adds encrypted backups, separated test and production data, staff access limits, and an access log.
Third-party guides report these are required for public apps and checked by automated tests.

requirements.item: Post-grant redirect to the app UI
requirements.detail: After approval, merchants must land in the app's UI, not a login page.
A third-party article says public apps must migrate to offline tokens that expire after 60 minutes and use a refresh token, before 1 Jan 2027.

scopes.effect: These touch protected customer data. Public apps need protected-data review (level 2 if name, email, phone or address is involved). Custom apps have access always.
Order data contains customer PII and falls under protected-data rules for public apps. By default only the last 60 days of orders are accessible.
Gives access to orders older than 60 days. It must be declared together with read_orders or write_orders and follow your app's approval requirements.

scopes.scope: read_apps, read_checkout_settings, read_customer_payment_methods, read_shopify_payments, read_payment_gateways, read_financial_kyc_information, etc.
scopes.effect: Shopify must approve these before you can declare them. Contact Shopify Support and explain your app and why it needs the scope.
Declare them in the app version, and merchants approve them at install. Request only what you use.

blockers.symptom: You can't find a way to create a custom app in the Shopify admin.
blockers.cause: Since 1 Jan 2026, new custom apps can't be created in the admin.
blockers.fix: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard and install it on the store.

blockers.symptom: You need to install on more stores than custom distribution allows, or charge through Shopify.
blockers.cause: Custom distribution is limited to one store or one Plus organization, has no Shopify billing, and can't be changed after you pick it.
blockers.fix: Decide on Public or Custom before you choose. If you need both, create a separate public app.

blockers.symptom: Customer name, email, phone or address fields come back null.
blockers.cause: Your public app isn't approved for the matching protected customer data scopes or fields.
blockers.fix: Submit a protected customer data request under API access requests in the Partner Dashboard.

blockers.symptom: You can't declare a scope labeled 'Shopify approval required'.
blockers.cause: Shopify has to approve these scopes first.
blockers.fix: Contact Shopify Support, describe your app and explain why it needs the scope, or remove the scope.

blockers.symptom: The review is rejected for an unexpected URL redirect during OAuth.
blockers.cause: After the grant, the app sends merchants to a login page instead of its UI.
blockers.fix: Redirect straight to the app UI after merchants accept the scopes.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect mismatch.
blockers.cause: The redirect URI isn't in the app's allowed redirection URLs.
blockers.fix: Add the exact Composio callback URL to the released app version.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must register your own app from the start and enter its Client ID and Client Secret in a Composio auth config. Composio uses per-shop URLs: authorize at https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize and exchange tokens at https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token. Add Composio's callback URL to the app's allowed redirection URLs. The default scope list includes customer and order scopes, which trigger protected-data review for public apps, so trim it. Composio also lists an S2S_OAUTH2 mode.

open_questions: No official install cap or user limit for unreviewed public apps was found.
The full official App Store listing requirements (privacy policy, support URL, logo, demo video, screenshots) were not verified.
It's unresolved whether a limited-visibility public app can be installed by direct link before full review.
The per-version redirect URL field in the Dev Dashboard is confirmed only by a community post.
The offline token expiry change (60-minute tokens by 1 Jan 2027) comes only from a third-party source.
Composio's catalog redirect URI (api/v1/auth-apps/add) differs from the callback seen in practice (api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). Use the one shown in your Composio auth config.
Review turnaround isn't stated officially; third-party figures range from 3 to 10 business days.
Built for Shopify and revenue-share thresholds were not verified.
